sentences.text: Natunaornis gigoura was an extinct flightless pigeon that lived on Viti Levu, the largest island in Fiji.
Fossil evidence includes a holotype tarsometatarsus and paratypes consisting of various wing and leg parts, though no skull parts are known except for a possible referred premaxilla.
The species name reflects its large size and proposed relationship to crowned pigeons of the genus Goura.
This species was only slightly smaller than the dodo and the Rodrigues solitaire.
Remains were discovered in Quaternary cave deposits in October 1998 and November 1999.
The species was first described in 2001.
The holotype is held in the Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa.
The genus name honors Natuna, an elder of the Volivoli people in the Sigatoka Valley where the fossils were found.
The species lived from the Late Pleistocene to the Holocene, between 0.129 and 0 million years ago.
